title: Sunrise staggered surge playbook (scratch)
content:
Context:
Personal scratchpad for a morning-first staggered release pattern for hosted inference (small traffic bursts, keep latency budget tight). Goal is a conservative, observable ramp that gives us signal fast and a simple fast rollback path.

High-level approach (one-liner):
- Start with a tiny anchor cohort (0.05% total), verify fast signal (1–3 min), then short bursts to 1%, 5%, 15% over a 90–120 minute window with fixed hold windows and explicit health gates.

Why morning-first?
- Ops/eng overlap availability during earliest hours in NA.
- Traffic predictable, slower growth to catch unstable regressions before peak.

Pre-launch (T-24h):
- Run smoke canary on staging that mirrors backend kernels (quantized path) — confirm perf parity within 10% latency.
- Confirm telemetry dashboards: modelErrors, modelLatencyP50/P95/P99, tokenCostPerReq, modelFallbackRate.
- Confirm oncall list and escalation Slack channel: #deploy-fastpath
- Validate rollback artifact ID and pin list. Document pinned model sha and container tag.
- Warm caches: run synthetic prefix calls to populate KV for high-volume clients (script: tools/warmup/warm_kv.sh)

Preflight checklist (15 mins before launch):
- [ ] All CI green for main and the deployment PR (link above).
- [ ] Infra capacity check: Dedicated pools show >= 2x expected burst headroom for the region (dashboard: infra/capacity).
- [ ] Routing rules baked: canary-route v2 defined and ready.
- [ ] Canary flags toggled off in staging, ready to flip in prod.
- [ ] Slack pinned message template prepared (see Templates section).

Launch timeline (local time: 07:00–09:30 PT example):
- 07:00 — flip anchor cohort to 0.05% (clients: internal beta + first-party devs). Hold 5 min quick health check window.
- 07:05 — if green, bump to 0.5% (hold 10 min).
- 07:15 — if green, bump to 1.5% (hold 15 min).
- 07:30 — bump to 5% (hold 20–30 min).
- 08:00 — bump to 15% (hold 30–45 min), then evaluate for wider release.

Notes on hold durations: shorter early holds let us iterate quickly, longer mid-stage holds capture slower signal (memory leaks, throughput saturation).

Gating metrics (immediate failure criteria — fail fast):
- Error budget: increase in modelErrorRate > 0.5% absolute AND > 3x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-min buckets => FAIL.
- Latency: P99 latency increase > 150 ms absolute AND > 50% relative for 3 consecutive minutes => FAIL.
- Cost signal: tokenCostPerReq jump > 30% persistent for 5 min => investigate (non-fatal initially).
- Fallbacks: modelFallbackRate > 1% absolute => FAIL (indicates degraded model variant).
- Token truncation / unexpected short outputs: spike in short-response rate > 2x baseline => WARN, consider limiting rollout.

Monitoring queries (copy/paste friendly):
- modelErrorRate (1m): sum(errors) / sum(requests) by service
- modelLatencyP99 (1m): histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(latency_ms_bucket[1m]))
- fallbackRate: sum(fallbacks) / sum(requests)
- shortOutputRate: sum(label_short_outputs) / sum(requests)
(Exact metrics live in dashboards; have these queries pre-saved).

Rollback/fast-abort steps (one-click ideal but list below manual):
1) Abort ramp: remove canary-route from traffic and route back to pinned model variant.
   - redwoodctl routing set --route canary-route --traffic 0 --target pinned:v2025-02-17
2) Re-pin clients if needed: apply per-tenant override for highest-risk customers.
   - curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/pins -d '{"tenant":"T123", "model":"pinned:v2025-02-17"}'
3) Revert code if root cause is infra/runtime (GH PR revert): 
   - gh pr revert 1876 --repo redwood-inference/service
4) Notify #deploy-fastpath with rollback note and incident label.

Escalation ladder (quick):
- On-call SRE (primary) -> Eng release owner -> Tech lead for runtime -> Product for customer comms.
- If >30% traffic impacted or >10% of customers seeing failures, open incident and page pager duty.

Post-launch notes to capture (first 2 hours):
- latency deltas per model variant and per-customer (top 5 by request volume).
- any increased retries from clients (clientRetryRate).
- observe token distribution per request to detect prompt blowups.
- write down weirdness in raw request/response around failing requests (copy raw logs).

Slack templates (short):
- Green progression: "Sunrise rollout: 5% -> PASS (P99 120ms, errors 0.02%). Proceeding to 15% in 30m unless flagged."
- Abort notice: "ABORT: Sunrise rollout paused at 1.5% due to P99 spike. Rolling back to pinned:v2025-02-17. See incident: JIRA-RT-4021"

Questions / uncertainties (notes to self):
- Does quantized path add transient cold-start on first few requests that could be mistaken for a regression? Add a synthetic warmup that mirrors "real" clients.
- Are regional routing fallbacks configured if a zone shows higher GC/latency? (check smart routing rules).
- How to safely escalate to Dedicated pool if hosted nodes exhibit memory pressure? Pre-script migration steps.

Playbook TODOs (next iterations):
- [ ] Add automated canary abort script that executes checks and can revert in one command.
- [ ] Build a tiny dashboard view that only shows the five gating metrics for the release owner.
- [ ] Create a per-tenant simulation harness to sanity-check pin overrides.

Snippets / handy commands (for quick paste):
- Check current routing: redwoodctl routes list --json | jq '.[] | select(.name=="canary-route")'
- Force route to pinned: redwoodctl routing set --route canary-route --traffic 0 --target pinned:v2025-02-17 && slack-send --channel #deploy-fastpath "Rollback done: pinned:v2025-02-17"

Notes-to-self sign-off (end):
- Keep communications concise. Use numbers not adjectives. If unsure, pause rollout and wait for telemetry to stabilize rather than pressing forward.
- Aim for reproducible actions (scripts) rather than manual clicks in console. Reduces human error.

Random small experiments to try later:
- Tiny traffic bursts with synthetic heavy prompts to exercise worst-case kernel paths, run before human-facing canary.
- Pair with cost-aware fallback: route cheap quantized variant for low-priority tenants automatically during ramp.

End of scratchpad.
